meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is wrong with you today?

examples.text: Отстань от меня, что ты ко мне пристала?
examples.trans: Leave me alone, why are you pestering me?

examples.text: Никогда не думал, что скажу эту фразу.
examples.trans: I never thought I would say this phrase.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well why, leave it here.

examples.text: А что эта женщина из моего прошлого здесь делала?
examples.trans: And what was that woman from my past doing here?

examples.text: Не волнуйся, ей здесь долго не продержаться.
examples.trans: Do not worry, she will not last long here.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.trans: Vitya, what is going on with us?
What is going on here with you?

examples.text: Что здесь происходит, я вас спрашиваю?
examples.trans: What is going on here, I am asking you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When love leaves, emptiness remains.
And besides, you are simply a pig.
What is wrong with you today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You started choosing other girls.
You are both owners of this restaurant.

examples.text: Можно я со своим шефом первый поговорю?
examples.trans: May I talk with my chef first?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прашивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am asking', paired with 'спросить'.

examples.text: Что здесь происходит, я вас спрашиваю?
examples.trans: What is going on here, I am asking you?
I'm asking you!
He always asks.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Well why, leave it here.
Why did she leave so pleased?

examples.text: Это ещё почему, гости же замёрзли.
examples.trans: Why is that, the guests got cold.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'call', paired with 'позвонить'.

examples.trans: Quiet, that is Dima calling right now.
Someone is ringing the doorbell there.
Take it, that is Kostya calling you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When love leaves, emptiness remains.
No one can fill it.
Well, or almost no one.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'complain'.

examples.text: Да я обязательно буду на вас жаловаться!
examples.trans: I will definitely complain about you!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и жаловаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and complain on time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'mess / chaos' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Почему мне люди звонят и жалуются, что здесь бардак?
examples.trans: Why are people calling me and complaining that there is a mess here?
We have a bit of a mess here.
There was total chaos in the room.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ещать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'promised', paired with 'пообещать'.

examples.text: Нам вообще обещали весь этот ресторан.
examples.trans: We were promised this entire restaurant.

examples.text: Я обещал и я всё сделал, а где Витя?
examples.trans: I promised and I did everything, and where is Vitya?
I promise you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не торопись, сначала надо всё обсудить.
examples.trans: Do not hurry, first we need to discuss everything.
These are all my people.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты мне всё понятно объяснил.
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you explained everything clearly to me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'made', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We will do everything at the highest level.

examples.text: Я обещал и я всё сделал, а где Витя?
examples.trans: I promised and I did everything, and where is Vitya?
We've done a lot.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When love leaves, emptiness remains.
No one can fill it.

examples.text: А в клубе ты был смелее.
examples.trans: At the club you were bolder.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, and where are my jeans?
And where are my jeans?

examples.text: Я обещал и я всё сделал, а где Витя?
examples.trans: I promised and I did everything, and where is Vitya?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А в клубе ты был смелее.
examples.trans: At the club you were bolder.
And besides, you are simply a pig.
You started choosing other girls.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Are you free right now, we need to talk.
Quiet, that is Dima calling right now.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, я сейчас поеду на работу.
examples.trans: Alright, guys, I will drive to work now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are doing', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.text: А что эта женщина из моего прошлого здесь делала?
examples.trans: And what was that woman from my past doing here?

examples.text: Опять ты, что я у тебя делаю?
examples.trans: You again, what am I doing at your place?

examples.text: Мы же с тобой вчера ничего не делали.
examples.trans: After all, you and I did not do anything yesterday.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello, dear Dmitry Vladimirovich.
Hello, Dima.
Hello, dear Kostya.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When love leaves, emptiness remains.
Well, or almost no one.

examples.text: А в клубе ты был смелее.
examples.trans: At the club you were bolder.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Между прочим, это у меня завтра важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: By the way, I am the one who has an important event tomorrow.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, у меня здесь важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: Hello, I have an important event here.
It's an important question.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'event' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Между прочим, это у меня завтра важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: By the way, I am the one who has an important event tomorrow.

examples.text: Витя, меня завтра на мероприятии не будет.
examples.trans: Vitya, I will not be at the event tomorrow.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, у меня здесь важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: Hello, I have an important event here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'really', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And you will manage it together.
What are you going to manage there?

examples.text: Не будешь ты ими управлять, ясно?
examples.trans: You will not manage them, is that clear?

meanings.en: actually, strictly speaking, as a matter of fact
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Правда, вообще-то это у меня здесь мероприятие.
examples.trans: Really, actually I am the one who has an event here.

examples.text: А вообще-то я ещё не решил.
examples.trans: Actually, I haven't decided yet.
Actually, this is my seat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если это угроза, она будет дорого вам стоить.
examples.trans: If that is a threat, it will cost you dearly.
You are both owners of this restaurant.
That is very funny and amusing.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Ты же сама не захотела быть со мной.
examples.trans: After all, you yourself did not want to be with me.

examples.text: Хотел сказать тебе большое спасибо за всё.
examples.trans: I wanted to say thank you very much for everything.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: А я тебе сказала, оставь, иначе я тебя уволю.
examples.trans: And I told you, leave it, otherwise I will fire you.
She said that the restaurant is closing tomorrow.

examples.text: Потом подошёл Дима и сказал то же самое.
examples.trans: Then Dima came up and said the exact same thing.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('very much, big').

examples.text: У нас сегодня, кажется, большой праздник.
examples.trans: It seems we have a big celebration today.
Thank you very much, Dima.

examples.text: Желаем тебя больше здесь не видеть никогда.
examples.trans: We wish never to see you here again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты мне всё понятно объяснил.
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you explained everything clearly to me.
Thank you very much, Dima.
Thank you for your loyalty.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No one can fill it.

examples.text: Ты же сама не захотела быть со мной.
examples.trans: After all, you yourself did not want to be with me.

examples.text: Если это угроза, она будет дорого вам стоить.
examples.trans: If that is a threat, it will cost you dearly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: What, excuse me?

examples.text: Вика, прости, я совсем не специально.
examples.trans: Vika, forgive me, I did not mean to at all.
Forgive me, I did not do it on purpose.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Прости меня, у тебя вечно из-за меня проблемы.
examples.trans: Forgive me, you always have problems because of me.
You cannot be afraid forever.
You're right, one cannot be afraid forever.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Прости меня, у тебя вечно из-за меня проблемы.
examples.trans: Forgive me, you always have problems because of me.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.trans: Of course, no problem, dear Kristina.

examples.text: Прости меня, у тебя вечно из-за меня проблемы.
examples.trans: Forgive me, you always have problems because of me.
That's not a problem.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When love leaves, emptiness remains.
What is wrong with you today?
Alright, let us go there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No one can fill it.

examples.text: У неё нет таких волос, как у меня.
examples.trans: She does not have hair like mine.

examples.text: Отстань от меня, что ты ко мне пристала?
examples.trans: Leave me alone, why are you pestering me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У неё нет таких волос, как у меня.
examples.trans: She does not have hair like mine.
That way you will gradually forget her.

examples.text: Я не хочу, чтобы он тебя видел здесь в таком виде.
examples.trans: I do not want him to see you here in this state.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты мне всё понятно объяснил.
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you explained everything clearly to me.

examples.text: Что тебе нужно, отстань от меня, поняла?
examples.trans: What do you want, leave me alone, understand?
I have already understood everything perfectly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No one can fill it.

examples.text: Ты же сама не захотела быть со мной.
examples.trans: After all, you yourself did not want to be with me.

examples.text: У нас сегодня, кажется, большой праздник.
examples.trans: It seems we have a big celebration today.

meanings.en: in advance, beforehand, ahead of time
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ранее').

examples.trans: After all, I warned you in advance!
Did you set all this up in advance?

examples.text: Мы купили билеты на поезд заранее.
examples.trans: We bought the train tickets in advance.

meanings.en: to warn, to give advance notice
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упреждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'warned', paired with 'предупредить'.

examples.trans: After all, I warned you in advance!
I warned you.
I am warning you for the last time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You started choosing other girls.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты мне всё понятно объяснил.
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you explained everything clearly to me.
Meet my friend Masha.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maxim, you are fired, go home.
Where's my toy car?
That's mine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.text: Да, а что я должен подумать?
examples.trans: Yes, and what am I supposed to think?

examples.text: Я должен часами ждать тебя там?
examples.trans: Am I supposed to wait for you there for hours?
Alright, then we keep working.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'before', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, но теперь я хочу миллион.
examples.trans: Yes, but now I want a million.
Yes, now I want a million.
Oh, I will call you back later.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'виниться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'apologize', paired with 'извиняться'.

examples.text: Друзья мои, я должен перед вами извиниться.
examples.trans: My friends, I must apologize to you.
I said sorry, didn't I?
Apologise to Dad.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'watch out / beware'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и беречься вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and watch out on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют беречься.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to watch out.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я хочу сегодня обновить наше меню.
examples.trans: I want to update our menu today.

examples.text: Немедленно шпинат убрать из нашего меню.
examples.trans: Immediately remove the spinach from our menu.

examples.text: Алло, наш адвокат только что умер.
examples.trans: Hello, our lawyer just died.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'drink', paired with 'выпить'.

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.trans: I'm drinking tea.
He doesn't drink.

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?
